sentences.en: Specially-made lanterns are hung outside each house to help the dead to find their way.
sentences.zh: 家家户户门外都挂着特制的灯笼，帮助亡灵找到回家的路。

article.en: A festival for the dead is held once a year in Japan.
article.zh: 日本每年举行一次祭奠亡灵的节日。

article.en: This festival is a cheerful occasion, for on this day, the dead are said to return to their homes and they are welcomed by the living.
article.zh: 这个节日是个欢乐的日子，因为在这一天，据说亡灵会返回家园，受到活着的人的欢迎。

article.en: As they are expected to be hungry after their long journey, food is laid out for them.
article.zh: 由于人们认为他们长途旅行之后会饿，所以为他们摆出了食物。

article.en: Specially-made lanterns are hung outside each house to help the dead to find their way.
article.zh: 家家户户门外都挂着特制的灯笼，帮助亡灵找到回家的路。

article.en: All night long, people dance and sing in the streets.
article.zh: 人们整夜在街上唱歌跳舞。

article.en: In the early morning, the food that had been laid out for the dead is thrown into a river or into the sea.
article.zh: 清晨，为亡灵摆放的食物被扔进河里或海里。

article.en: It is considered unlucky for anyone living to eat it.
article.zh: 因为活着的人吃这些食物被认为是不吉利的。

article.en: In towns that are near the sea, the tiny lanterns are placed into the water when the festival is over.
article.zh: 在靠海的城镇，节日结束后，头天晚上挂在街上的小灯笼被放入水中。

article.en: Thousands of lanterns slowly drift out to sea, guiding the dead on their return journey to the other world.
article.zh: 成千上万只灯笼缓缓漂向大海，为亡灵返回另一个世界的旅程引路。

article.en: Crowds of people stand on the shore watching the lanterns drifting away until they can be seen no more.
article.zh: 成群的人站在岸边，看着灯笼漂走，直到再也看不见为止。
